title: Embedding config sensitivity and holdout sanity suite
creator: Ana Rivera
description:
Problem: Recent config and model swaps have caused subtle embedding/reranker degradations that only show up on narrow cohorts. We've had near-miss incidents where a config tweak reduced recall@100 for support queries by ~4% but average metrics barely changed.

Goal: Build a deterministic "config sensitivity" offline harness that runs a curated holdout + cohort probe suite across permutations of model + quantization + batching + KV-cache policies. The harness should: (1) produce per-cohort recall/precision/MRR/nDCG deltas with bootstrap CIs, (2) compute distributional drift stats for embedding spaces (cosine shift, KS, PSI), (3) export a compact regression signal used by CI gate and the console alerting pipeline.

Scope: offline harness (unit + integration tests) + a lightweight CI step that runs fast probes on PRs + a nightly exhaustive sweep for release candidates. Not in scope: online canary rollout wiring (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run full holdout suite (10k queries, 50k corpus samples) end-to-end in staging and produce a reproducible report
Per-cohort metrics (recall@10, recall@100, mrr, nDCG) and bootstrap 95% CIs are computed and stored as time-series
Embedding distribution diagnostics: cosine mean/variance, KS p-value vs baseline, PSI computed and flagged if > 0.2
Config-delta matrix exported in JSON summary used by CI: for each config pair produce delta, CI, and verdict (OK | WARN | FAIL)
Fail-gates: any cohort with recall@100 regression > 2.5% with p<0.05 marks CI job as FAIL
Nightly sweep runs and uploads report to the Embedding QA dashboard and creates automated issues when FAIL is detected
technical_notes: Use existing replay pipeline to fetch anonymized query logs; add deterministic sampling for holdout cohorts
Implement bootstrap resampling (n=1000) for robust CIs; use stratified bootstrap per cohort
Drift metrics: cosine shift distribution (delta mean), two-sample KS on cosine similarity, PSI on binned similarities
Optimize runtime by reusing cached embeddings when only config (e.g., batching, kernel) changes and not the model weights
Provide a compact JSON summary schema (fields: cohort, baseline_config, new_config, metric, delta, ci_low, ci_high, p_value, verdict)
Integrate with CI via a small Docker image that runs the fast probe subset (1k queries, 5k corpus) under PR changes
Edge cases: when corpus changes (new documents index) fallback to conservative verdict and surface to engineers
test_plan: Unit: runner logic, JSON schema validation, bootstrap statistics functions
Integration: run harness end-to-end on synthetic corpus with known perturbation (we will inject a 5% embedding noise on subset to validate detection)
CI probe: add to PR pipeline with a 10-minute timeout — must produce PASS/WARN/FAIL summary
Nightly: run exhaustive sweep; compare nightly deltas to previous 7 days to reduce false positives
Monitoring: create Grafana panels for delta trends, false-positive rate, and nightly job success/failure rates
